newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ENGLAND SUFFER FROM "GORMLESS" RUN OUTS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND SUFFER FROM "GORMLESS" RUN OUTS.

text.p: England suffered an embarrassing day against Mashonaland on Tuesday, with two run outs to dismiss Nick Knight and John Crawley being described by coach David Lloyd as "gormless".
Off-spinner Robert Croft helped to spare England's blushes to a degree by making top score of 66 not out as the touring team reached 175 for nine at the close of the first day of the four-day match.
England, who lost a one-day game against a Zimbabwe President's XI on Sunday, slumped to 27 for four at one stage as a rookie county pacer bowler plunged them into trouble.
Sussex's James Kirtley had taken four for 44 when bad light forced an early end to the day. A three-hour rain stoppage earlier meant 35 overs were lost in total.
Kirtley had England captain Mike Atherton caught behind for two and bowled Nasser Hussain for two also in an opening spell of two for 14 from five overs.
With Bryan Strang knocking out Alec Stewart's leg stump when he had scored only one, England were reeling at seven for three.
Opener Knight was foolishly run out as he was sent back after starting on a third run and, with Crawley later run out for a confident 25, England slipped to 94 for seven at one point.
Only Croft's perfectly-judged innings -- he hit 21 in the final two overs of the day -- prevented England from being completely humbled.
"Good players playing poorly," was the verdict of Lloyd.
"You can't disguise that we have had a poor batting day but it doesn't worry me at all. But we will have to look at basic areas that we will have to improve in. The run outs were gormless."
Kirtley, who took a hat-trick on his debut for Mashonoland against Matabeleland last week, had mixed feelings about his performance in what was only his 11th first-class match.
"I know which flag I will be flying when the tests and one-day internationals start but it was nice to do well," he told reporters.
Kirtley can still post career best figures in the innings. His previous best is five for 51 for the TCCB X1 against the South African A side in the last English season.

England omitted paceman Chris Silverwood, all-rounder Ronnie Irani and wicketkeeper Jack Russell from their 11, suggesting Stewart may be given the wicketkeeper's role in the first test starting in Bulawayo on December 18.
